claims.text: Short-range chemical order varies among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Variations in short-range chemical order govern the mechanical-property differences among these alloys.
Changes in local chemical order alter lattice distortions.
Altered lattice distortions modulate dislocation mobility.
Changes in dislocation mobility affect yield strength and ductility.
Selective changes in Cr or Mn concentration modify the balance of local chemical interactions and the extent of short-range chemical order.
Atom probe tomography can characterize the relevant local atomic arrangement and short-range chemical order.
Transmission electron microscopy can assess the resulting local lattice distortions.
Enhanced short-range order pins dislocations more effectively.
More effective dislocation pinning increases yield strength.
More effective dislocation pinning reduces ductility.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, alloys with enhanced short-range order will have increased yield strength and decreased ductility.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, alloys with diminished short-range order will have reduced strength and potentially improved ductility.
The proposed relationship applies primarily to consistently processed, single-phase FCC alloys and may not apply to multiphase materials or substantially different processing histories.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property response to altered short-range order depends on specific local atomistic interactions.
